samples.summary: Verbatim, uncapped forwarding of upstream response bodies now happens on every CLI command — untrusted upstream content flows unfiltered into agent-consumed stderr
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:169-179) prints `JSON.stringify(res.data, null, 2)` in full whenever `res.data.error.code` happens to be a string. `isErrorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:76-85) validates only that one field: everything else in the body — an arbitrarily long `error.message`, sibling fields, a stack trace, an internal identifier — is echoed verbatim. The sibling non-envelope path deliberately hardens the same data (`MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE = 500` at formatter.ts:90 and the `startsWith('<')` HTML rejection at formatter.ts:117); the verbatim path has neither cap nor filter, so the hardening is bypassed simply by including `error.code`. Before this delta only six commands could reach that path; this delta routes ~25 more `!res.ok` branches (docs.ts:80/107/121/139/157, notes.ts:40..117, slides.ts:45..122, cells.ts:29/69/95/147, tabs.ts:20/53/79, files.ts:90/110/128/146, api-keys.ts:22/36/50, sheets-import.ts:91, sheets-export.ts:43) through it. Attack: a compromised, malicious, or MITM'd server (`--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` / config profile is free-form and the URL scheme is not pinned, config.ts:90-94) answers any request with `{"error":{"code":"SESSION_EXPIRED","message":"<megabytes of text, or instructions aimed at the reading agent>"}}`. packages/cli/README.md explicitly positions this stderr line as what AI agents branch on, so the payload lands directly in an agent's context, and it can also spoof CLI-reserved codes (TYPE_MISMATCH, CONFIRMATION_REQ) to steer behaviour. Note JSON.stringify does escape control chars, so ANSI/terminal escape injection is not possible — the vector is content/volume, not terminal control. Suggested fix: apply the same length cap (and a field whitelist of `code`/`message`) on the verbatim path.

samples.summary: Upstream server-supplied error text is now echoed to stderr by every command, widening backend information disclosure into terminals/CI logs
samples.evidence: `upstreamMessage`/`upstreamDetail` (formatter.ts:104-127) splice the upstream body's `message` (up to 500 chars) into the CLI's error output. Before this delta, ~25 commands emitted only `HTTP <status>` and disclosed nothing from the response body; after it, every one of them (including the auth-sensitive `api-keys create|list|revoke`, api-keys.ts:22/36/50) prints whatever the server put in `message`. Nest has no global exception filter in this repo (see the comment at formatter.ts:96), so 500 bodies carry the raw framework/driver message, and `class-validator` bodies can echo submitted values — this text then lands in shell history, CI job logs, and agent transcripts. I could not find a concrete case where the backend echoes a credential (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.service.ts:73-81 emit only generic strings), so this is a disclosure-surface widening rather than a confirmed leak.
searchedFor: grep 'error: { code' in packages/backend/src (no documented envelope emitted server-side)

samples.summary: Path parameters are interpolated into request URLs without encoding, allowing caller-supplied ids to redirect the authenticated request to a different endpoint
samples.evidence: `revokeApiKey` builds `${server}/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}/api-keys/${id}` (http-client.ts:385) with the raw CLI argument, and the same pattern appears in getDocument/updateDocument/deleteDocument (199-205) and the cells/tabs helpers (330-361). `downloadFileDocument` (254) shows the intended `encodeURIComponent`. A doc-id or key-id of `../../../../auth/me` (or one containing `?`/`#`) is normalised by fetch, so the request — carrying the user's bearer token or API key — is sent to a different path on the configured server than the command claims. This delta rewires exactly these commands' failure paths through `forwardUpstreamError`, which now prints the resulting foreign endpoint's body, making the mis-targeted request observable output rather than a silent `HTTP <status>`. Impact is bounded: WorkspaceScopeGuard (packages/backend/src/api/v1/workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-36) still enforces membership, so this is not an authz bypass — it matters mainly when ids come from untrusted data in an agent workflow.

samples.summary: Error matrix now contradicts itself on authentication failures: 401/403 still documented as exit 2 / UNAUTHORIZED while the new rows route every non-envelope failure to exit 1 / HTTP_ERROR
samples.evidence: The two rows added at docs/design/cli.md:1039-1040 say any failed request whose body is not the envelope reports `HTTP_ERROR` with exit 1, but the pre-existing row immediately below still promises `Backend 401/403 → exit 2, code UNAUTHORIZED, "Authentication failed. Run `wafflebase login`"`. In the implementation, `forwardUpstreamError` sets `process.exitCode = 1` unconditionally (formatter.ts:175) and `outputError` likewise (formatter.ts:62); nothing in packages/cli/src maps 401/403 to exit 2 or to `UNAUTHORIZED` (grep for `UNAUTHORIZED`/`exitCode = 2` in packages/cli/src returns nothing). An agent or script that branches on the documented auth signal will never see it and cannot distinguish "re-authenticate" from "bad input", which is a weakened auth-failure signal rather than a bypass. The delta made this authoritative by adding conflicting rows to the same table.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists (forwardUpstreamError prints JSON.stringify(res.data) verbatim at formatter.ts:173-176 whenever isErrorEnvelope's single check on error.code passes, formatter.ts:80-84, while the sibling path caps at MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE=500 and rejects HTML, formatter.ts:90/117-120). But the claimed security impact is refuted by a counterexample in the same code paths: every success branch already forwards the identical server-controlled body verbatim and completely uncapped into the agent-consumed stream — cells.ts:30 and docs.ts:87/108/122/140/158 call output(res.data, ...), which is format() -> formatJson() = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) (formatter.ts:31-33, json.ts:1-3), with no length cap, no field whitelist and no HTML/content filter, at ~60 call sites. A compromised/MITM'd server therefore needs no error.code to push megabytes or agent-directed text into the agent's context; it answers 200 with that payload as the command result. The 500-char cap is documented as a readability heuristic for framework/HTML bodies (formatter.ts:87-90, 115-117), not a trust boundary, so nothing security-relevant is 'bypassed' by the verbatim path. There is also no secret exposure (res.data is the remote body or the client's own fixed SESSION_EXPIRED envelope, http-client.ts:156-164, never CLI credentials) and, as the finding itself concedes, JSON.stringify escapes control chars so no terminal/ANSI injection is possible. What remains — a CLI printing what its user-configured server returned — is not an authorization gate, secret leak, injection sink or broken crypto check, and is not blocking under the Security rubric.
